pr.title: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert

raw_findings.body: The expression is evaluated unconditionally (before checking optimized_pagination), so previously working audit-log requests now crash with AttributeError -> HTTP 500, breaking the endpoint for API-key/token consumers.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled AttributeError turns all non-member authenticated requests into 500 responses regardless of the new query parameter.
raw_findings.impact: The expression is evaluated unconditionally (before checking optimized_pagination), so previously working audit-log requests now crash with AttributeError -> HTTP 500, breaking the endpoint for API-key/token consumers.
raw_findings.root_cause: New gating logic dereferences `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without handling the None member case defined by the RpcUserOrganizationContext model.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard for None membership, e.g. `organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access`, and only evaluate it when `use_optimized` is true.
raw_findings.title: AttributeError when organization_context.member is None on every GET request
raw_findings.trigger: Any GET to the audit-log endpoint where the requester is not a superuser and organization_context.member is None, e.g. requests authenticated via an org API key, org auth token, or active staff without org membership (RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None`).

raw_findings.body: Bypasses Sentry's convention of gating privileged behavior on `is_active_superuser(request)` (as used elsewhere in sentry.api.bases.organization), enabling the untested 'advanced' pagination path — explicitly commented as allowing 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' — based solely on a persistent user flag and a client-controlled query parameter.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Privilege gate is weaker than the codebase convention, allowing non-elevated sessions to activate an alternate, less-safe pagination code path.
raw_findings.impact: Bypasses Sentry's convention of gating privileged behavior on `is_active_superuser(request)` (as used elsewhere in sentry.api.bases.organization), enabling the untested 'advanced' pagination path — explicitly commented as allowing 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' — based solely on a persistent user flag and a client-controlled query parameter.
raw_findings.root_cause: New privileged code path is enabled by a client-controlled query parameter combined with the raw is_superuser database flag rather than the active-superuser session check.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the query-param controlled branch entirely, or gate it on `is_active_superuser(request)` and an option/feature flag instead of `request.user.is_superuser` and a GET parameter.
raw_findings.title: Superuser gate uses raw is_superuser flag instead of active-superuser check for query-param controlled paginator switch
raw_findings.trigger: A user whose account has the is_superuser flag set (but without an active, elevated superuser session) or any member with has_global_access sends `?optimized_pagination=true`.

raw_findings.body: Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, which is not caught by the BadPaginationError handler in Endpoint.paginate, producing an unhandled 500. The comments claiming 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' are false.
raw_findings.evidence:
if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:
            # Special handling for negative offsets - enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds
            # This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level
            start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination
            stop = start_offset + limit + extra
            results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
raw_findings.failure_mode: Crafted cursor input causes an unhandled AssertionError and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error.
raw_findings.impact: Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, which is not caught by the BadPaginationError handler in Endpoint.paginate, producing an unhandled 500. The comments claiming 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' are false.
raw_findings.root_cause: New code deliberately passes negative offsets into QuerySet slicing based on an incorrect assumption about Django ORM behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete the negative-offset branch and reject negative cursor offsets with BadPaginationError, mirroring OffsetPaginator's `if offset < 0: raise BadPaginationError` guard.
raw_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset slicing raises AssertionError on Django querysets
raw_findings.trigger: A qualifying user requests the audit-log endpoint with `optimized_pagination=true` and a crafted cursor containing a negative offset (e.g. `cursor=0:-5:0`), which Cursor.from_string accepts.

raw_findings.body: `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError, so every non-empty optimized page 500s. Additionally `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value that build_queryset compares against the `datetime` column, unlike DateTimePaginator which converts via timestamp/multiplier, so cursor filtering would be wrong even if the key worked.
raw_findings.failure_mode: TypeError on every page with results; incorrect SQL cursor comparison semantics for datetime keys.
raw_findings.impact: `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError, so every non-empty optimized page 500s. Additionally `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value that build_queryset compares against the `datetime` column, unlike DateTimePaginator which converts via timestamp/multiplier, so cursor filtering would be wrong even if the key worked.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new paginator copies Paginator's numeric key/value conversion while its only call site orders by a datetime column.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Reuse DateTimePaginator's get_item_key/value_from_cursor (or subclass DateTimePaginator) instead of copying the numeric Paginator implementations.
raw_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses integer key semantics but is invoked with order_by='-datetime'
raw_findings.trigger: Any successful request through the optimized branch of OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint that returns at least one row: build_cursor calls get_item_key on each result, where `getattr(item, 'datetime')` is a datetime object.

raw_findings.body: Rows are fetched from offset 0 but build_cursor/_build_next_values still compute the next cursor from the raw negative `cursor.offset` (e.g. `next_offset = offset + limit`), so subsequent pages skip or duplicate rows instead of the request being rejected. The added comment claiming 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' is false — this changes behavior of the core paginator for all endpoints.
raw_findings.evidence:

        results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent pagination state produces skipped/duplicated results for malformed cursors across every BasePaginator-backed endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: Rows are fetched from offset 0 but build_cursor/_build_next_values still compute the next cursor from the raw negative `cursor.offset` (e.g. `next_offset = offset + limit`), so subsequent pages skip or duplicate rows instead of the request being rejected. The added comment claiming 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' is false — this changes behavior of the core paginator for all endpoints.
raw_findings.root_cause: Fetch offset is clamped to zero while all downstream cursor arithmetic continues to use the unclamped negative offset, and the is_prev path still passes negative offsets to queryset slicing.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Revert to `stop = offset + limit + extra` and reject negative offsets explicitly (raise BadPaginationError), rather than clamping only the fetch offset.
raw_findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward offsets while cursor building still uses the raw offset
raw_findings.trigger: Any endpoint using BasePaginator subclasses (DateTimePaginator, Paginator, etc.) receives a forward cursor with a negative offset such as `100:-50:0`, which Cursor.from_string parses successfully.

raw_findings.body: Segment trees with redirect depth between 1000 and 10000 that previously resolved correctly now terminate early, so spans are attached to the wrong intermediate set and segments are split/mis-joined. The removed comment documenting this exact limitation makes the behavior change invisible to future readers.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Deep traces silently produce incorrectly joined segments with no log or metric indicating truncation.
raw_findings.impact: Segment trees with redirect depth between 1000 and 10000 that previously resolved correctly now terminate early, so spans are attached to the wrong intermediate set and segments are split/mis-joined. The removed comment documenting this exact limitation makes the behavior change invisible to future readers.
raw_findings.root_cause: Loop bound silently tightened by 10x with the caveat comment removed, changing correctness envelope without documentation or detection.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either restore the 10000 bound or keep 1000 with a restored comment documenting the correctness trade-off, and emit a signal when the loop exhausts without converging.
raw_findings.title: Redirect-chain loop bound reduced from 10000 to 1000 and explanatory comment deleted
raw_findings.trigger: A trace whose redirect map contains a chain deeper than 1000 hops (deeply nested span trees ingested child-first).

raw_findings.body: The Python-side `max_segment_spans` limit check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, so this hardcoded 1000 is now the only enforcement. The configuration parameter is silently dead: operators tuning `max_segment_spans` get no effect, and the default (1001) already disagrees with the Lua constant (1000).
raw_findings.evidence:

end
raw_findings.failure_mode: Configuration knob silently stops working; eviction threshold cannot be tuned and mismatches the documented default.
raw_findings.impact: The Python-side `max_segment_spans` limit check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, so this hardcoded 1000 is now the only enforcement. The configuration parameter is silently dead: operators tuning `max_segment_spans` get no effect, and the default (1001) already disagrees with the Lua constant (1000).
raw_findings.root_cause: Enforcement moved from configurable Python code into the Lua script with a hardcoded constant that ignores the existing `max_segment_spans` setting.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the span-count limit into the script as an ARGV parameter from SpansBuffer instead of hardcoding 1000.
raw_findings.title: Eviction threshold hardcoded to 1000 in Lua, diverging from configurable max_segment_spans
raw_findings.trigger: SpansBuffer is constructed with a non-default `max_segment_spans` (constructor parameter, default 1001); any segment reaching >1000 spans.

raw_findings.body: Span data is now dropped with no metric or log at all, so operators lose the ability to detect oversized segments and quantify data loss introduced by the new eviction path; dashboards/alerts on the removed metric silently go dark.

raw_findings.trigger: A segment exceeds the span-count limit; previously this incremented `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and logged an error, now the Lua zpopmin eviction silently discards the lowest-timestamp spans.

finding.failure_mode: Configuration knob silently stops working; eviction threshold cannot be tuned and mismatches the documented default.

validated_findings.body: The expression is evaluated unconditionally (before checking optimized_pagination), so previously working audit-log requests now crash with AttributeError -> HTTP 500, breaking the endpoint for API-key/token consumers.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled AttributeError turns all non-member authenticated requests into 500 responses regardless of the new query parameter.
validated_findings.impact: The expression is evaluated unconditionally (before checking optimized_pagination), so previously working audit-log requests now crash with AttributeError -> HTTP 500, breaking the endpoint for API-key/token consumers.
validated_findings.root_cause: New gating logic dereferences `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without handling the None member case defined by the RpcUserOrganizationContext model.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Guard for None membership, e.g. `organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access`, and only evaluate it when `use_optimized` is true.
validated_findings.title: AttributeError when organization_context.member is None on every GET request
validated_findings.trigger: Any GET to the audit-log endpoint where the requester is not a superuser and organization_context.member is None, e.g. requests authenticated via an org API key, org auth token, or active staff without org membership (RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None`).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 71 verbatim shows `organization_context.member.has_global_access` evaluated unconditionally. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (model.py:346). When member is None, AttributeError occurs before the `use_optimized` check, crashing all requests where member is None.

validated_findings.body: Bypasses Sentry's convention of gating privileged behavior on `is_active_superuser(request)` (as used elsewhere in sentry.api.bases.organization), enabling the untested 'advanced' pagination path — explicitly commented as allowing 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' — based solely on a persistent user flag and a client-controlled query parameter.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Privilege gate is weaker than the codebase convention, allowing non-elevated sessions to activate an alternate, less-safe pagination code path.
validated_findings.impact: Bypasses Sentry's convention of gating privileged behavior on `is_active_superuser(request)` (as used elsewhere in sentry.api.bases.organization), enabling the untested 'advanced' pagination path — explicitly commented as allowing 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' — based solely on a persistent user flag and a client-controlled query parameter.
validated_findings.root_cause: New privileged code path is enabled by a client-controlled query parameter combined with the raw is_superuser database flag rather than the active-superuser session check.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the query-param controlled branch entirely, or gate it on `is_active_superuser(request)` and an option/feature flag instead of `request.user.is_superuser` and a GET parameter.
validated_findings.title: Superuser gate uses raw is_superuser flag instead of active-superuser check for query-param controlled paginator switch
validated_findings.trigger: A user whose account has the is_superuser flag set (but without an active, elevated superuser session) or any member with has_global_access sends `?optimized_pagination=true`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 73 shows `if use_optimized and enable_advanced` where enable_advanced uses `request.user.is_superuser` (persistent flag) not `is_active_superuser(request)` (session check). The codebase convention (organization.py:70) uses is_active_superuser for privilege gates. This allows non-elevated superuser sessions to activate the advanced path via query param.

validated_findings.body: Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, which is not caught by the BadPaginationError handler in Endpoint.paginate, producing an unhandled 500. The comments claiming 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' are false.
validated_findings.evidence:
if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:
            # Special handling for negative offsets - enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds
            # This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level
            start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination
            stop = start_offset + limit + extra
            results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
validated_findings.failure_mode: Crafted cursor input causes an unhandled AssertionError and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error.
validated_findings.impact: Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, which is not caught by the BadPaginationError handler in Endpoint.paginate, producing an unhandled 500. The comments claiming 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' are false.
validated_findings.root_cause: New code deliberately passes negative offsets into QuerySet slicing based on an incorrect assumption about Django ORM behavior.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Delete the negative-offset branch and reject negative cursor offsets with BadPaginationError, mirroring OffsetPaginator's `if offset < 0: raise BadPaginationError` guard.
validated_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset slicing raises AssertionError on Django querysets
validated_findings.trigger: A qualifying user requests the audit-log endpoint with `optimized_pagination=true` and a crafted cursor containing a negative offset (e.g. `cursor=0:-5:0`), which Cursor.from_string accepts.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 877-882 show negative offset passed directly to queryset slicing: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` where start_offset is cursor.offset when negative. Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises AssertionError, not caught by BadPaginationError handler.

validated_findings.body: `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError, so every non-empty optimized page 500s. Additionally `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value that build_queryset compares against the `datetime` column, unlike DateTimePaginator which converts via timestamp/multiplier, so cursor filtering would be wrong even if the key worked.
validated_findings.failure_mode: TypeError on every page with results; incorrect SQL cursor comparison semantics for datetime keys.
validated_findings.impact: `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError, so every non-empty optimized page 500s. Additionally `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value that build_queryset compares against the `datetime` column, unlike DateTimePaginator which converts via timestamp/multiplier, so cursor filtering would be wrong even if the key worked.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new paginator copies Paginator's numeric key/value conversion while its only call site orders by a datetime column.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Reuse DateTimePaginator's get_item_key/value_from_cursor (or subclass DateTimePaginator) instead of copying the numeric Paginator implementations.
validated_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses integer key semantics but is invoked with order_by='-datetime'
validated_findings.trigger: Any successful request through the optimized branch of OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint that returns at least one row: build_cursor calls get_item_key on each result, where `getattr(item, 'datetime')` is a datetime object.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 838-843 show get_item_key uses `int(math.floor(value))` on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The endpoint passes order_by='-datetime', so self.key='datetime' and value is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator converts via strftime first.

validated_findings.body: Rows are fetched from offset 0 but build_cursor/_build_next_values still compute the next cursor from the raw negative `cursor.offset` (e.g. `next_offset = offset + limit`), so subsequent pages skip or duplicate rows instead of the request being rejected. The added comment claiming 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' is false — this changes behavior of the core paginator for all endpoints.
validated_findings.evidence:
start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset
        stop = start_offset + limit + extra
        results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent pagination state produces skipped/duplicated results for malformed cursors across every BasePaginator-backed endpoint.
validated_findings.impact: Rows are fetched from offset 0 but build_cursor/_build_next_values still compute the next cursor from the raw negative `cursor.offset` (e.g. `next_offset = offset + limit`), so subsequent pages skip or duplicate rows instead of the request being rejected. The added comment claiming 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' is false — this changes behavior of the core paginator for all endpoints.
validated_findings.root_cause: Fetch offset is clamped to zero while all downstream cursor arithmetic continues to use the unclamped negative offset, and the is_prev path still passes negative offsets to queryset slicing.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Revert to `stop = offset + limit + extra` and reject negative offsets explicitly (raise BadPaginationError), rather than clamping only the fetch offset.
validated_findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward offsets while cursor building still uses the raw offset
validated_findings.trigger: Any endpoint using BasePaginator subclasses (DateTimePaginator, Paginator, etc.) receives a forward cursor with a negative offset such as `100:-50:0`, which Cursor.from_string parses successfully.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 182 shows `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For is_prev=True with negative offset, offset passes through unclamped to queryset slicing, causing AssertionError. For is_prev=False, offset is clamped but cursor arithmetic at line 192 still uses raw offset, causing inconsistent pagination state.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Either restore the 10000 bound or keep 1000 with a restored comment documenting the correctness trade-off, and emit a signal when the loop exhausts without converging.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 30 shows loop bound changed from 10000 to 1000 (`for i = 0, 1000 do`). The removed comment documented this limitation. Traces with redirect depth 1000-10000 will now terminate early, potentially mis-joining segments.
